# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Incident window:** 2026-03-14 02:14–03:59 UTC (log ends 03:59; no recovery observed in the data).
**Status at handoff:** ongoing, not mitigated.
**Sources:** `logs/gateway.log` (node-3 of 3), `logs/worker.log`, `deploys.csv`.

## Root cause

Gateway deploy `dep-4471` (author a.novak, 02:12:00–02:14:00Z, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") switched the gateway connection pool to one connection per request without increasing pool size.

The config reload is logged directly:

```
02:12:12.820Z INFO config reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41.234Z INFO config generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed
02:13:41.234Z INFO config   gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
02:13:41.234Z INFO config   gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
```

Pool size stayed at 20. Before the change the pool ran `in_use=3..9 idle=17..11 waiting=0`; after it pinned to `in_use=20 idle=0` with the wait queue growing monotonically (12 up to 271; last stats line at 03:55 shows `waiting=172` and still rising). The companion change `upstreamMs 2000 -> 2500` holds each connection 25% longer and compounds the exhaustion.

Every failure is the same error, 530 occurrences, each paired 1:1 with a 503:

```
ERROR pool req-17907 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 74)
```

Plus 213 `WARN pool ... acquire slow: waited 835ms for a connection`.

This is not an upstream fault. The 503s spread evenly across all four backends — accounts-svc 133, catalog-svc 133, billing-svc 132, orders-svc 132 — which is the signature of the gateway starving locally rather than any one dependency failing.

## Impact window

First 503 at `02:14:18.972Z` (`req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms`), 19 seconds after the deploy finished. Clean for the full preceding hour (01:00–02:10, 0 errors in 574 requests).

Error rate by 10-minute bucket: 0% through 02:10, then 30/117 in the 02:10 bucket (partial, deploy mid-bucket), then steady at roughly 50/132 — about 38% — from 02:20 to the end of the log at 03:59. On-call was paged at `03:21:05Z`: `error_rate 5m avg is 71%`. The 71% figure is the 5-minute average over `/v1/*` traffic; the 38% figure includes `/health` checks, which continued to succeed.

## Rollback

Roll back `dep-4471`. Revert config generation 119 to 118, or at minimum set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`. If the pool-isolation goal needs to be preserved, the pool must be resized well above peak concurrency first — at the observed queue depth the current size 20 is off by more than an order of magnitude.

Loop in a.novak; they own the change.

Deploys ruled out: `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) landed 27 minutes after the error rate was already flat, and the 503s hit all four upstreams equally rather than billing alone. `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20) produced no change in error rate. `dep-4470` (worker, 00:48) is 80 minutes before onset, inside the clean period.

## Two caveats for the next shift

**Only one of three gateway nodes is in evidence.** The log header reads `node-3 of 3`. Nodes 1 and 2 were not reviewed. Confirm the config generation and error rate on those before or during rollback.

**Workers have a separate, unrelated problem.** All 1080 worker jobs in the window finished OK, zero errors, and the worker DB pool was idle throughout (`size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0`, unchanged from 01:00 to 03:50). But job duration ramps linearly across every job type — average 437ms at 01:00 rising to 2087ms at 03:30, a constant +330ms per 30 minutes with `db_wait` flat at 5ms. There is no inflection at 02:14, and the ramp is already underway when the log opens, so it predates the gateway change and is not caused by it. All six job types show the same absolute +2000ms offset, which points at accumulation inside the job runner rather than contention. Nearest prior deploy is `dep-4470` (worker, 00:48, j.tanaka, "retry backoff for webhook jobs") — plausible on timing, but the ramp affects all job types, not just webhook, so treat it as a lead and not a conclusion. Worth a separate ticket. Also note the worker runs 4 replicas and only one log was available; check whether the other three show the same slope.

**One data-quality note:** the logs are dated 2026-03-14, not last night (2026-08-26). Either the capture is stale or these are the wrong files. Verify before acting on the rollback.
